title: Evaluating Large Language Models: A Comprehensive Survey

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating coreference resolution accuracy with gendered pronouns (e.g., Winogender, WinoBias), assessing translation accuracy of gendered nouns, measuring performance differences in relation extraction, and checking for stereotypical preferences in sentence pairs.

Assessing sentiment analysis scores across race-related sentences (e.g., EEC), measuring deviation from neutrality in Natural Language Inference (NLI) tasks, and multiple-choice stereotype association tests.
Measuring the variation in sentiment scores of sentences when age-related vocabulary is changed (e.g., replacing 'young' with 'old').
Measuring deviation from neutrality in NLI tasks using ethnic names and assessing stereotypical biases in sentence pair prediction tests.
Evaluating NLI tasks for deviation from neutrality and using sentence pairs to determine if language models prefer stereotypical sentences related to religion.
Assessing implicit hate speech, evaluating generated text for offensiveness or harmful agreements, and performing intra-sentential prediction tests for stereotypes.
Measuring stereotypical bias through sentence pair preferences (e.g., CrowS-Pairs) and evaluating models on implicit hate speech detection tasks.
Jointly assessing bias scores in model responses for offensiveness, harmful agreements, and occupational associations, as well as testing stereotypical associations.
Evaluating open-ended language generation prompted by political ideology topics using metrics like sentiment and toxicity (e.g., BOLD benchmark).

Using multiple-choice question answering datasets customized for socio-cultural factors (e.g., CBBQ assessing biases around disease, educational qualification, household registration, and region in Chinese contexts).
